title: Inject LocalDayClock into ParentDashboardAggregator instead of hardcoding SystemLocalDayClock
why: compute({DateTime? now}) documents now as 'pass explicitly for testability', and every other metric (pace, engagement, recent-completions window) honors it — but the streak sub-computation always builds StreakStateProvider with a hardcoded SystemLocalDayClock(), which reads real DateTime.now() regardless of the now argument. The accompanying test cannot control this and is forced to call real DateTime.now() to seed matching streak_events (quoted comment at lines 119-121 explains exactly why), making that test a genuine wall-clock dependency and leaving a live day-boundary race: if the wall clock ticks past local midnight between the caller choosing now and StreakStateProvider's internal clock read, currentStreak/maxStreak reflect a different 'today' than the rest of the ParentDashboardData snapshot.
recommendation: Accept an optional LocalDayClock clock constructor parameter (default const SystemLocalDayClock()), pass it into StreakStateProvider, and derive it from the aggregator's own now so compute(now: ...) fully determines the snapshot including streak.
acceptance_criteria: A new unit test overrides the injected clock (not real DateTime.now()) and asserts currentStreak/maxStreak for a fixed 'today', replacing the wall-clock seeding at parent_dashboard_aggregator_compute_test.dart:118-122.
The TQ-6 hermetic-test grep (no DateTime.now() outside core/time) passes for this test file.
mergedFrom: Replace DateTime.now().toUtc() with a fixed clock in parent_dashboard_aggregator_compute_test.dart's streak test
